page: Microsoft Azure D32pds_v5 is an ARM-based general-purpose server instance powered by an Ampere Altra ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor. It features 32 dedicated physical cores running at 3.0 GHz with one thread per core, eliminating hyperthreading overhead. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of RAM, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per core. Local storage is bundled, offering 1229 GB of local disk capacity, and the instance is Premium Storage capable under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Benchmark data indicates average multi-core and memory performance. The instance achieved a stress-ng multi-core score of 57203.87 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 12912.0. Memory bandwidth is measured at 166.64 GB/sec for large uncached reads and 75.94 GB/sec for large uncached writes. Database operations are supported by a Passmark database score of 21065.71 and Redis SET performance of 40.63 million operations per second. However, single-core performance is a notable tradeoff, with a weak Geekbench single-core score of 1125.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 1822.59.

The ARM64 architecture lacks x86-specific instruction sets such as AVX, AVX-512, and AMX, which limits its utility for advanced vector or matrix calculations. This is reflected in poor large-scale LLM inference speeds, yielding only 2.31 tokens per second for text generation on a 70B model. Conversely, the server demonstrates solid capabilities in software compilation with a Geekbench clang score of 28132.0 and static web serving at 31.62 GB/sec throughput. This profile makes the instance qualitatively cost-efficient for scale-out workloads, multi-threaded applications, web serving, database hosting, and general-purpose ARM64 development.
